title: Aza'raan Language Guidebook

sections.title: How to Use This Language Guide
sections.text:
Tab 01  |  How to Use This Language Guide
The origin registry consists of exactly 52 user-selected hieroglyphs, including the origins of the glottal stop and click. The five written-era alphabet totals are Ancient 52, Archaic 49, Classical 44, Traditional 32 and Modern 21. Modern has 55 readings.
Every glyph is traced to its original hieroglyph. Nine designated source glyphs win their merged modern family contours; the other lines retain their own dated historical forms until merger.
Members of any family with multiple readings all take accents, even the family’s primary reading; only true singleton families are unaccented.
Return to contents: Contents

sections.title: Before Aza’ra: Proto-Oceanic and Uxrowo
sections.text:
Tab 02  |  Before Aza’ra: Proto-Oceanic and Uxrowo
Uxrowo preserves the pictured signs and glyph meanings assigned in the old hieroglyph register. The Proto-Oceanic-inspired Kaʻaheʻanua strand supplies a contrasting speech tradition. The two do not literally inherit every feature of their real-world analogues. Cultural exchange with other Aza’ran peoples produces further layers of borrowing rather than a single isolated fusion.
Create independent etymological records for Uxrowoiye and Kaʻaheʻanua, then a contact ledger for Kaluseban and other named communities. For every shared noun, specify the giver and receiver, the route of contact, use in speech or writing, and dated evidence if present. Unrecorded details remain reconstructions.
The parent languages must remain separately documented. Do not call pre-Cataclysm Uxrowoiye 'Modern Aza’raan'.
Return to contents: Contents

sections.title: 1351 BCE: Convergence and Language Contact
sections.text:
Tab 03  |  1351 BCE: Convergence and Language Contact
The Cataclysm in 1351 BCE brought survivors and neighboring peoples into closer contact. Aza’raan grew when Uxrowoiye and Proto-Oceanic-inspired communities needed to speak together. Trading, rescue, marriages and multi-species settlements also exposed it to the languages and naming practices of other original Aza’ran peoples.
Model a five-stage process: encounter, code switching, shared trade register, family transmission and local standardization. Add donor-tagged vocabulary instead of presuming that everyone abandons their own speech. Distinguish this language event from the later political destruction of Belavadös.
1351 BCE marks the Cataclysm, not an overnight full alphabet or all-at-once language invention. Contact effects are hypotheses until supported by original documents.
Return to contents: Contents

sections.title: Proto-Aza’raan: Hieroglyphic Signs
sections.text:
Tab 04  |  Proto-Aza’raan: Hieroglyphic Signs
Proto-Aza’raan uses exactly 52 ORIGINAL HIEROGLYPHS taken from the Uxrowo source register. These are parent signs, not glyphs invented for later eras. They preserve the source shape, phonetic clue, and provenance.
For each of the 52 hieroglyphs, record original sign, source sound/IPA and all descendants by era. Glottal 𓃪 and click 𓐎 are origin signs; later signs are not new origins.
Do not substitute later alphabetic glyphs into the origin column or use modern combining accents in Proto.
Return to contents: Contents

sections.title: Ancient Aza’raan: First Almost Letters
sections.text:
Tab 05  |  Ancient Aza’raan: First Almost Letters
Ancient Aza’raan has 52 separately identifiable historical signs, all traced one-to-one to the 52 original hieroglyphs. The source hieroglyph remains fixed, while its Ancient descendant is a different script form.
Keep an independent Ancient descendant for each origin. The Archaic era is added immediately after Ancient; the first mergers are introduced there, not retroactively into Ancient.
A blank or unapproved descendant shape must be labeled pending rather than replaced by a fabricated historical form.
Return to contents: Contents

sections.title: Archaic, Classical and Traditional Aza’raan
sections.text:
Tab 06  |  Archaic, Classical and Traditional Aza’raan
Archaic Aza’raan has 49 alphabet letters; Classical has 44; Traditional has 32. The Proto and Ancient source register still includes 52 original lineages.
Archaic reclassifies the glottal and click as special signs, outside the later alphabet counts, and contains one letter merger. Classical contains five more mergers; Traditional contains twelve. Independently document the morphology of each descendant before it merges.
The TZ/TAZ descendant of 𓎱 stays distinct in Ancient, Archaic and Classical before merging into the T family descended from 𓆠 in Traditional.
Return to contents: Contents

sections.title: Phonology and Sound Change
sections.text:
Tab 08  |  Phonology and Sound Change
Aza’raan sound history follows Proto source hieroglyphs and five written eras: Ancient (52), Archaic (49), Classical (44), Traditional (32), and Modern (21). The 52 origin records remain permanent; independent descendant forms persist until their dated mergers.
For every sound change record the starting value, conditioning environment, approximate era, affected speech community and written outcome. Use the same mark meaning across letter families: acute raises/fronts, grave lowers/backs, circumflex broadens or diphthongizes, caron turns or affricates, macron lengthens, breve reduces, diaeresis separates a glide, tilde nasalizes, ogonek adds EH, cedilla softens, dot above brightens or voices, and stroke/bar fortifies or devoices.
The five-stage chronology is a design specification for this invented language. Do not present the accents as evidence of a real-world script lineage.
Return to contents: Contents

sections.title: The Egyptian Picture Roots
sections.text:
Tab 09  |  The Egyptian Picture Roots
The 52 exact origin hieroglyphs are the author-selected parent signs, not a set of new alphabet characters. See the complete original five-column source table preserved in the combined guide and the expanded 52-row lineage register.
Protected parent signs: 𓆠→T; 𓋜→N; 𓈌→B; 𓇰→K; 𓊲→O; 𓈚→I; 𓆣→E; 𓄣→A; 𓆇→S. Their descendants establish the pre-accent glyph for every reading in the resulting family.
Historical descendants from other parents stay in the chart until the merger, rather than disappearing from earlier eras.
Return to contents: Contents

sections.title: From Pictures to Linear Strokes
sections.text:
Tab 10  |  From Pictures to Linear Strokes
The writing-system progression is origin hieroglyph → Ancient descendant (52) → Archaic descendant (49) → Classical descendant (44) → Traditional descendant (32) → Modern family glyph (21).
For each original sign preserve a row that records the shape lineage, active era, merger into another family if applicable, source sound, and whether a later shape has author-approved artwork.
Where shapes have not yet been supplied, explicitly mark a descendant as pending. Never present the original hieroglyph copied unchanged as a new invented descendant.
Return to contents: Contents

sections.title: Accented Family Glyphs and Special Signs
sections.text:
Tab 11  |  Accented Family Glyphs and Special Signs
There are only two letter-display categories: inherited family glyphs and accents when applicable. Glottal, click and syllable-emphasis signs are separate special signs.
Every Modern reading belonging to a multi-reading family uses the same family contour plus a meaningful accent. The main reading must also carry an accent; the five singleton families remain bare.
The keyboard and font need single family outlines, accent placement, and the four special signs. No other letter-attachment form category is part of the system.
Return to contents: Contents

sections.title: Compound Signs and Diphthongs
sections.text:
Tab 12  |  Compound Signs and Diphthongs
Compounds and diphthongs are documented as historical sound developments within their letter families. They do not create extra independent letters in the 21-letter Modern inventory.
Maintain a dated descendant for an originally distinct glyph until the point at which it merges; then represent the later reading with the inherited family contour and an accent.
The TZ/TAZ origin 𓎱 must remain separately visible through Classical before joining 𓆠 in Traditional.
Return to contents: Contents

sections.title: Word-Changing Marks and Emphasis
sections.text:
Tab 13  |  Word-Changing Marks and Emphasis
The twelve productive accents distinguish family readings; a family with variants never uses an unaccented letter, including for its first or default reading.
Use Unicode combining marks on Latin transliterations (NFC where available). The four special signs are apostrophe U+0027 for glottal stop, ¡ U+00A1 for click, < U+003C for previous-syllable emphasis, and > U+003E for next-syllable emphasis.
The glottal apostrophe is separate from the acute mark composed using a keyboard modifier; the previous/next signs are literal angle brackets.
Modern accent register
The twelve productive marks retain one meaning across every letter family. They begin as Ancient and Classic merger marks, are shortened in Traditional cursive and are normalized with Latin Unicode in Modern Aza’raan.
Special signs: ‘ glottal /ʔ/; ¡ click /ǃ/; < previous-syllable emphasis; > next-syllable emphasis. Full keyboard sequences are in modern-azaaraan-keyboard-layout.json.
Return to contents: Contents

sections.title: Sentence Order and Information Structure
sections.text:
Tab 14  |  Sentence Order and Information Structure
Aza’raan allows subject, action and affected participant to change order when particles preserve their relationships. Conversational emphasis, not fixed English order, decides which element comes first.
Example grammar template: [topic marker] + person + [agent marker] + action + [target marker] + object. The bracketed descriptors are pedagogical slots, not invented canonical words.
Do not claim a complete translation until its particles have confirmed lexical forms.
Return to contents: Contents

sections.title: Particles, Aspect and Evidentials
sections.text:
Tab 15  |  Particles, Aspect and Evidentials
The original generator supplies dozens of particle functions, from topic and role to evidentiality, emotion and silence. The developing common language may recruit older words from either founding strand and, where needed, calque or borrow social distinctions from neighboring peoples. These are paths for believable change, not proof that a specific ethnic community invented a given particle.
A candidate particle needs source community, semantic function, earliest historical phase, shift in use, independent or accent form, and contrast with established particle words. Do not derive pronouns by copying English categories.
Generated forms begin as proposals and never overwrite an established dictionary entry without explicit review.
Return to contents: Contents

sections.title: Pronouns and Identity Morphology
sections.text:
Tab 16  |  Pronouns and Identity Morphology
Identity-linked pronouns are created from social descriptions and grammatical role particles. A speaker chooses what is appropriate to the person and community; the grammar does not assign identity from appearance.
The source pronouns guide records unresolved forms. Keep a two-column history of the identity term and the corresponding role-bound form, with optional neutral reference where speakers have agreed to it.
Do not turn unfinished lexical slots into invented canonical pronouns.
Return to contents: Contents

sections.title: Nouns, Verbs and Derivations
sections.text:
Tab 17  |  Nouns, Verbs and Derivations
Derivation should remain visible across eras. A word for a bridge can give rise to a verb for linking, a profession for bridge-tending and a metaphor for reconciliation.
Test contact-induced compound formation separately from inherited derivations and new coinages. Aza’raan may adapt borrowed consonant-final forms with vowels in ordinary speech while preserving old proper names in writing. Log donor name, original source evidence, adapted stem, affix, era and approval flag.
Older synonyms may coexist when their history or speaker community differs.
Return to contents: Contents

sections.title: Kaluseban Naming: Korean and French
sections.text:
Tab 18  |  Kaluseban Naming: Korean and French
Kaluseban has an established original Aza’ran identity and six ancestral bloodlines. The author-specified Korean and French inspirations apply to Kaluseban name design. Across mixed communities, Kaluseban speech can influence Aza’raan names, local woodland terminology and styles of address, with each borrowing remaining a modeled possibility until the lexicon is approved.
Keep the Kaluseban naming guide distinct from general Aza’raan phonology. For loan candidates capture original Kaluseban meaning, town and period of contact, phonetic adaptation, and whether the name stays untranslated.
Yermifana and Gyerfima are illustrative naming proposals, not words verified in either source language.

Name construction: (C)V.CV.CV; usually 3-5 syllables. Fuse a Korean-inspired meaningful root and French-inspired root. Transform both for the fictional Kaluseban phonology; avoid simply attaching two unchanged real words.

sections.text:
Tab 19  |  Tamhiogal Naming: Arabic and Polish
Tamhiogal is an original people in the strict register. The author’s Arabic and Polish naming inspirations inform Tamhiogal proposals, not the etymology of Aza’raan as a whole. Regional seafaring, shared families and trade councils provide plausible contact routes between Tamhiogal and speakers of Aza’raan.
Record donor form, original community usage, maritime or civic contact route, Aza’raan sound accommodation and manuscript evidence status. Reject any assumption that an entire community has one immutable dialect.
Do not automatically associate name sound with religion, personality or morality.
Naming guide for TTRPG and MMORPG characters
Influences: Arabic, Polish. Arabic-inspired emphatic or pharyngeal-feeling transitions are adapted for fiction; Polish-inspired sibilants, soft consonants and clusters are smoothed for Tamhiogal speech. Never require difficult clusters for every speaker.
Name construction: CV.CCV.CV or CV.CV.CCV; 2-4 syllables. Meaning root + water or family root; the second root may modify the first. Endings -a, -in and -eya are optional regional inventions.

sections.title: Dril’thar Naming: Egyptian, Navajo and Taa
sections.text:
Tab 20  |  Dril’thar Naming: Egyptian, Navajo and Taa
Dril’thar is a distinct people with underwater-breathing bloodlines. The author’s Egyptian and Navajo inspirations are naming design analogies. Coastal contact could enrich shared terms for navigation, depth and maritime travel, but the existing source does not specify the actual words or sound shifts.
Distinguish underwater cultural terminology, shore-market loanwords and personal names. Mark unverified shapes, sound changes and translated roots as proposed, then compare with the Uxrowoiye picture-root record before designing a new letter.
Exact real-language etymologies require verification by qualified sources before presenting them as facts.
Naming guide for TTRPG and MMORPG characters
Influences: Ancient or Old Egyptian, Navajo (Diné Bizaad), Taa (!Xóõ / !Xoon). Egyptian transliteration inspires consonant-rich pictorial ancestry, Navajo inspires controlled vowel length, nasality, tone and selected glottalic contrasts; Taa supplies the click articulation model. No literal Navajo or Taa words are copied.
Name construction: Optional CLICK + CV.CV or CV.CV.CV; do not require a click in every name. Honor name = optional click onset + one or two fictional roots + community ending. A click may also appear medially; ceremonial and everyday names can differ.
Constructed semantic roots: khe = river memory; sena = refuge; maru = glimmer; naki = ancestral path; tsu = listening (all constructed Dril’thar roots).
All Dril'thar name traditions belong to Dril'thar communities. Taa click symbols indicate distinct sounds, not decoration. No direct Egyptian-era vowel pronunciation is claimed.
Click guide: ǀ dental; ǃ alveolar; ǁ lateral; ǂ palatal; ʘ bilabial. These are consonant sounds, not decorative symbols or punctuation. In Dril’thar names, click choice can distinguish names. Clicks are optional in everyday names; do not force all lineages to use every articulation.
A consonant click may combine with voicing, nasality or other articulatory accompaniment, but no particular Dril’thar phonemic inventory is approved yet. The proposed examples use plain click place symbols and leave full dialectal phonetics for later author review.
The five-place click inventory is a phonological inspiration from Taa (!Xóõ), not a claim that fictional Dril’thar contains real Taa words. Old Egyptian is largely known from consonant-based writing, so modern Egyptological pronunciation conventions are not reliable vowel transcriptions of ancient speech. Navajo has meaningful vowel length, nasality, tone and glottalic consonant distinctions.

sections.title: Other Peoples and the Multilingual Contact Atlas
sections.text:
Tab 21  |  Other Peoples and the Multilingual Contact Atlas
CANON UPDATE | Earth-language university canon: Aza'raan universities maintain courses covering every Earth language, including living spoken and signed languages, historical languages, endangered traditions and documented reconstructions. Such courses prepare generations of Earth-keeper families to study Earth's societies and customs. This is a curricular addition, not a revision of Aza'raan letter counts or grammar.
CANON UPDATE | Historical underworld place names from Aramaic-based drafts are removed from active use. No replacements are invented until original Aza'raan word-formation and historical-script rules produce approved names.
Aza’raan is spoken amid many original peoples, including Kaluseban, Azrahai, Gandirosha, Panolima, Gwynis, Geisamahi, Dril’thar, Tamhiogal, Jaspey, Aburata, Deorbasun and Volsarii. Every one can influence it through contact without losing its own language. The companion atlas identifies two foundational streams and twelve contact streams, with source evidence separated from reconstructed possibilities.
Use Language/azaaraan_multilingual_contact_atlas.json to compare contact domains, plausible donor routes, provisional onset and vowel palettes, and evidence status. Naming, dialects, professions and rituals must be attributed to people and historical circumstances, not treated as inevitable inherited traits of their species. The eight proposed additional playable species remain proposals only.
The people names are established, but the suggested loan categories and phoneme palettes are not canonical facts. No playable people should be assumed linguistically homogeneous.

Supplement: Other Peoples, Physical Traits and Bloodlines
Physical reference for race selection and character naming. No changes have been made to Aza’raan grammar, letter inventory, historical stages or glyph system. The following appearance records distinguish strictly registered species from older, documented peoples and mixed communities.
Dril'thar
Small to modestly sized amphibious people, usually about one to four feet tall, with sinewy limbs, damp protective skin, webbed hands and feet, and often a powerful prehensile tail. Sensory fins or frills can frame the head. Large reflective eyes, color-shifting patterns, and luminous markings permit both speech and visual expression. They can move upright or on four limbs; moisture is essential to their health.
Grassland: Light sky blue, pale tan or sun-washed gold surfaces adapted to open wet meadows. Legs remain strong for leaping and traversing shallow water.
Lush Forest: Moss green, bark brown and lichen gray coloring; fine rootlike patterns help bodies blend into shaded wet woodland.
Marsh: Peat brown, slate gray and murky green mottling, often with a denser protective skin coating for stagnant wetlands.
Rainforest: Vivid emerald, sapphire or violet skins carrying bright bioluminescent rainlike markings and pronounced sensory frills.
Ocean: Ocean lineages may be slightly larger, with elongated swimming profiles, reflective seafoam or deep blue skin, and strong tails.
Reef: Brilliant reds, turquoise, luminous pink and textured coral-like patterning; fins and webbing support reef-water movement.
Kaluseban
Tall, slender, graceful magic-dependent humanoids with features that vary markedly among bloodlines. Skin may range from pale ivory through earth green and brown to deep sapphire. Eyes glow faintly in the color of their affinity, while fine hair can shimmer or float in dense ambient magic. Appearance should communicate personal lineage, not a single uniform skin color.
Psionic: psionic light in the eyes or temple markings can be an individual appearance cue.
Swamp: Wetland greens and browns with reed-like markings are characteristic possible looks. The historic text describes woodland and marsh-linked ancestors, but not every detail of this current label.
Arcane: Luminous pale or violet skin and shifting magical markings are among the approved options for an arcane lineage.
Dark: Low-light, shadow-touched coloring and dim luminescence can occur in this bloodline.
Stone: Source describes granite, sandstone and muted moonstone coloration, crystalline highlights, and markings reminiscent of stone inscriptions.
Oceanic: Pearlescent aquamarine or tide-blue color and water-adapted accents are approved visual options.
Azrahai
Original Aza'ran draconic people whose living anatomy includes scales, a powerful tail, clawed hands, facial ridges and, where appropriate to lineage, wings. Bodies range from heavy mineral-armored to long and streamlined. Ancient records call these same people Azh’raim; their modern name is Azrahai.
Noitzideq: Tall with layered green or blue-green scales, gold and dark speckles, feather-edged aerodynamic wings, and a muscular tail.
Saelftum: Massive, volcanic-adapted build with charcoal or black scales, amber and red accents, broad wings, horns and molten-looking fissures.
Jazwed: Coarse red-green iridescent scales, crystal clusters, dense muscular frame and shorter gliding wings adapted to heat.
Khoalaros: Long aquatic body with dark reflective scales, bioluminescent veins, webbed extremities, dorsal fins and swimming-capable wings and tail.
Gauksneth: Pale sand-colored crystalline scales, slim limbs and long sail-like wings suited to arid terrain.
Tuorszom: Gray, brown and black layered scales with mineral streaks, protective plates, and broad climbing hands and feet.
Taudinax: Dark iridescent scales, semi-translucent patches, silent wings, elongated fingers and a flexible tail.
Gouxelq: Deep blue metallic scales, crystal protrusions on shoulders and knuckles, heavy frame and broad flight wings.
Vautaces: Smooth ruby-red and cream scales with radiant crystal edging, long fingers, elegant wings and fine facial ridges.
Panolima
People whose bodies visibly reflect one of five elemental affinities, rather than a separate generic Elementaris species. Some are solid as stone, some carry ember patterns, others appear fluid, airy or illuminated by magical energy. Their silhouettes and voices may change with the environment; none of those forms should be mistaken for a separate current species.
Earth: Bark or stone textured skin, mosslike hair, weighty build, earthy fissures and a deep resonant voice.
Fire: Glowing ember veins, heatlike shimmer and hair that can suggest flame; specific color and physiology vary.
Water: Fluid, reflective skin and flowing hair or limbs that resemble currents; water effects need not imply constant liquid anatomy.
Air: Light, wind-swept features and shifting translucency, with clothing or hair that seems moved by unseen breezes.
Aether: Luminous magical auras, irregular light patterns and other non-elemental arcane features.
Jaspey
Jaspey are recognized as one people with three established forms, Mosscap, Gloomtail, and Rotcap. Each form has identifiable surface markings or anatomy. Their shared underlying body plan is not specified in the surviving current reference, so no extra height, limb count, or facial anatomy is invented here.
Mosscap: A moss-textured head or crown, with soft green-brown highlights.
Gloomtail: A shadow-adapted tail or low-light markings.
Rotcap: Dark fungal or decay-associated patterning.
The three Jaspey form appearances are approved. Their shared underlying body plan is not specified.
Deorbasun
Tall to towering magical shapeshifters, sometimes feline or beastlike, whose physiques vary from muscular to lithe. Fur, scales or earth-toned skin, reflective eyes, wings, tails or other animal features vary according to the individual's soul bond. No single default animal form applies to every member.
Open Soul-Animal: This is an open choice, not a preset wolf, cat or bird subtype. Record the person’s initial appearance and update markings or silhouette only after the true soul bond is established.
Gandirosha
Wiry or lithe agile figures, roughly three to six feet tall in the detailed source, with softly luminous skin and shifting freckle-like or sigil markings. Hair can range from honey and copper to chestnut, jade and gold. Eyes may glow subtly when magic is active; layered clothes and charms suit travel and performance.
Gwynis
Dream-born people with forms ranging from tall, shadow-touched silhouettes to luminous figures with weightless hair and shifting auroral features. Their eyes may appear to perceive several layers of reality. Intangibility and visual fluidity vary with magic and should not be assigned as a compulsory permanent body type.
Geisamahi
Small, upright, ferret- or stoatlike people with compact wiry bodies, elongated muzzles, expressive eyes, twitching whiskers and opposable thumbs. Fur may be brown, russet, orange, snow white or patterned. Their movement is nimble and acrobatic, and they often carry small belts and handmade tools.
Tamhiogal
Amphibious aquatic people with dramatic betta-fish coloration: brilliant blues, violets, teals, reds and shifting iridescence. On land they have scaled humanoid legs and arms, bioluminescent jellyfish-like hair, reflective eyes and scales at the face and neck. In water, gills, webbing, dorsal fins and a long caudal fin become prominent. They need hydration and tidal energy.
Aburata
Infernal magical beings with a humanoid and a quadrupedal equine-inspired form. Humanoid skin can resemble obsidian, molten iron or violet stone, marked by ember veins and living sigils. Curved or bladelike horns, fire-bright or voidlike eyes, varied hair and a prehensile tail distinguish individuals. The equine form adds a muscular horse-like trunk and hooved legs.
Volsarii
Ethereal four-armed people with elongated ear horns, sensitive antennae, iridescent skin and luminous or nebula-like eyes. Hair can look like liquid light, drifting mist or fine feathers. They pass through several lives in service to Nyxarion; during the final life they develop wings. No fixed number of lives is established.
Zirramunis
Compact, densely muscled humanoids with thick bones, strong forearms, calloused hands and skin ranging from granite gray and earth brown to ember-red. Their eyes shine in jewel-like shades. All genders may wear decorated beards, rings and braids as family or achievement records. The source does not name separate biological subtypes.
Garuraqets
Fine-boned, slender, magic-dependent winged people with iridescent skin in lilac, silver, mint and pale blue. Luminous hair may carry petals or glimmers. Their wings can resemble butterfly, dragonfly, leaves or living light; these are documented variations in wing morphology, not four separately approved species.
Butterfly-winged: Broad patterned wing membranes; source-documented wing morphology, not a separate species.
Dragonfly-winged: Fine transparent wings with a slender veined structure; source-documented morphology.
Leafwoven-winged: Leaflike wing outlines and botanical texturing; source-documented morphology.
Bioluminescent-winged: Wings patterned with active light; source-documented morphology.
Iamhazira
Very tall, heavily muscled people built for endurance. Skin ranges from charcoal gray and ochre to muted green, with scars or war paint carrying personal histories. Tusks may bear rings or carvings. Eyes often resemble embers or dark steel, hair is thick and braided, and ears are elongated or battle-nicked. No current source supplies an approved biological bloodline list.
Kalus’aan
Documented Aza’raan and Kaluseban mixed-ancestry community. Their Aza’raan cranial ridges, slender limbs, silver, blue, or green eyes and copper-to-auburn hair may mingle with Kaluseban color shifts, luminous marks, mineral textures, water-adapted accents, or forest and shadow features. The six documented Kalus’aan expressions are Arcane, Starborne, Wildroot, Tideborn, Stonebound, and Umbral; they are not six separate species. Appearance differs with the family and the particular Kaluseban bloodline.
Arcane: Gold, ivory or violet glow with shifting magical markings on skin and fingers.
Starborne: Pale blue, silver or amethyst tones with star-like reflections in the eyes.
Wildroot: Earthy barklike patterns, vine motifs and green-brown skin variation.
Tideborn: Pearl-blue or aquamarine skin, subtle webbing and currentlike hair.
Stonebound: Granite or sandstone skin accents, mineral shimmer and etched patterns.
Umbral: Dark skin with phosphorescent veins or shadowlike symbols.
Kalusogal
A documented Tamhiogal and Tideborn Kaluseban mixed community. Land forms retain smooth scaled cheeks and limbs, glowing eyes and kelplike bioluminescent hair. Aquatic forms show a streamlined tail fin, elbow and spine fins, and richly colored blue, crimson and violet scales. The two parental ancestries account for variation without requiring an invented separate bloodline list. This is Tamhiogal and Kaluseban ancestry, not an Aza’raan heritage or a separate founding species.
Aza’zira
Documented Aza’raan and Iamhazira mixed-ancestry community. Individuals blend Aza’raan facial proportions, psionic markings, and reflective eyes with Iamhazira height, powerful musculature, endurance traits, braids, strong jaw structure, and sometimes tusk features. Complexion may extend beyond the unmixed pale-to-lightly-tanned baseline where that parental lineage is visible. Individuals may retain copper or auburn hair, or express their Iamhazira family’s tones and scar or ornament customs.
Aza’raan
Aza’raan with Kaluseban ancestry: Kalus’aan is the established name for this mixed-ancestry community. Their Aza’raan cranial ridges, slender limbs, silver, blue, or green eyes and copper-to-auburn hair may mingle with Kaluseban color shifts, luminous marks, mineral textures, water-adapted accents, or forest and shadow features. The six documented Kalus’aan expressions are Arcane, Starborne, Wildroot, Tideborn, Stonebound, and Umbral; they are not six separate species. Appearance differs with the family and the particular Kaluseban bloodline.
Aza’raan with Deorbasun ancestry: An Aza’raan descendant of a Deorbasun family may keep pale-to-lightly-tanned Aza’raan skin and auburn or copper hair while expressing more pronounced reflective eyes, feline or other soul-animal hints, a heavier mane, unusual ear contours, tail, fur patches, claw-like nails, or rare wing features. The Deorbasun soul-animal bond is individually expressed and cannot be assigned a standard animal or fixed bloodline by appearance alone. No separate canonical community name has been established.
Aza’raan with Zirramunis ancestry: These descendants may be shorter or more densely built than a typical Aza’raan, with strong forearms, compact musculature, prominent bone structure, mineral-glinting eyes, stone-colored accent markings, and thick hair or beard growth. Copper and dark auburn hair and the silver, blue, or green Aza’raan eye spectrum can persist, with jeweled or metallic notes from Zirramunis heritage. No distinct mixed-species name or special fixed subtype is confirmed.
Aza’raan with Iamhazira ancestry: The historically documented Aza’zira community blends Aza’raan facial proportions, psionic markings, and reflective eyes with Iamhazira height, powerful musculature, endurance traits, braids, strong jaw structure, and sometimes tusk features. Complexion may extend beyond the unmixed pale-to-lightly-tanned baseline where that parental lineage is visible. Individuals may retain copper or auburn hair, or express their Iamhazira family’s tones and scar or ornament customs.
Aza’raan with Gandirosha ancestry: These descendants can retain the typical pale or lightly tanned Aza’raan complexion, copper or auburn hair and silver, blue, or green eyes, while expressing greater agility, a more compact or lithe build, freckles that resemble luminous sigils, more mobile facial expression, or colorful hair highlights associated with Gandirosha ancestry. These are variable family traits, not a separate named species or mandatory personality features.
Aza'raans are generally tall, slender and graceful, with long limbs and a very pale to slightly tanned complexion. The usual unmixed skin-color range resembles fair to lightly tanned complexions seen among Italian, Slavic and Balkan human populations, without implying any shared Earth ethnic identity. Copper, deep copper, auburn and dark auburn are the most common hair colors. Brown appears sometimes, while black and blonde are rare. Silver, blue and green eyes are common, often with a distinctly oceanic shape, occasionally dual-toned or subtly reflective. High oceanic-style cheekbones, a slightly angular brow with shallow paired ridges, and long ears swept backward are defining traits. Ear tips range from moderately pointed to dramatically sharp and elongated, with individual variation. Some Aza'raans bear faint freckles, subtle psionic luminescence, or wave-like ritual markings. Kaluseban, Deorbasun, Zirramunis, Iamhazira and Gandirosha ancestry can introduce additional color, stature, ear, hair, eye, animal-associated, or magical characteristics; such variation does not redefine the typical unmixed appearance.
The complete naming templates and source distinctions appear in the accompanying species atlas and JSON register.
Race Appearance Canon Update | 11 October 2026
Author-approved race appearance canon is synchronized with Aza_ra_All_Races_and_Mixed_Azaaraan_Heritages.txt and the shared race registry. These are corrections to people and character creation, not a revision to Aza’raan linguistic grammar or writing.
Dril'thar is the single, timeless name for the amphibious species and its six environmental bloodlines. Azh’raim is the ancient name of the draconic people; Azrahai is their modern name, simplified gradually over time without a new species arising.
Jaspey form appearances: Mosscap has a moss-textured head or crown with soft green-brown highlights. Gloomtail has a shadow-adapted tail or low-light markings. Rotcap has dark fungal or decay-associated patterning. All three are approved.
Aza’raans: very pale to lightly tanned complexion, chiefly copper through dark-auburn hair, brown hair sometimes, black and blonde hair rarely. Silver, blue or green eyes are common. Family variations can derive from Kaluseban, Deorbasun, Zirramunis, Iamhazira and Gandirosha heritage.
Pix, pointed ears and the maternal protector bloodline
Pix family appearance canon: Pix is a transgender man who can pass as human despite his visibly pointed, backward-swept ears. The childhood name 'Pix' came from those conspicuous ears, which his parents explained as an old inherited abnormality. Pix and his father have the tell-tale pointed ears. Pix's mother, Jacob and Clarahmizah have ordinary-looking human ears without points. Pix's mother eventually explains that much of the protector bloodline shared by her and Clarahmizah has Gandirosha and Zirramunis ancestry, and many descendants lost the conspicuous Aza'raan ear shape. Pix inherited the unmistakable ears through his father. The absence of pointed ears does not erase anyone's Aza'raan lineage or protector heritage.
